newsitem.title: USA: Motorola picks McCann-Erickson ad agency.
newsitem.headline: Motorola picks McCann-Erickson ad agency.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Thursday it chose McCann-Erickson Worldwide for global advertising of its consumer products, which include its cellular telephones and pagers.
The electronics giant said its 1997 spending on consumer advertising would exceed $100 million.

Motorola said in a statement it looked to the New York-based advertiser, which is owned by the Interpublic Group of Cos Inc, for a "quantum leap improvement in its relationship with its valued customers."
"We share Motorola's passion for building its brand in the hearts and minds of millions of consumers around the world," McCann-Erickson CEO John Dooner said.
The selection of McCann-Erickson by Motorola followed a three-month, worldwide review. The advertiser has previously done work for Motorola.

Motorola opted for the one-agency approach "to better focus our enthusiasm to relate to our consumers," said Rick Darnaby, a corporate vice president, global brand management, for the Schaumburg-based company that had 1996 sales of $28 billion.

"With one agency, we can better deliver a consistent message, strong brand develompment and the kinds of consolidated efficiencies and effectiveness that are the hallmarks of compaigns designed for the consumer marketplace," he said.
